answer: Running a farm therefore means funding each extra identity through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent pays once and never again. Because the age is read from the quill checkpoint rather than self-declared, the trellis audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 6 epochs old on the anchor ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. That is 32 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
